topic: WorkCanvas Studio: Framework-Neutral Browser Automation Workflow Samples for AI Agents

key_points: Primary source: open collection of realistic business-interface samples for browser workflow automation
Two samples: Standard HTML inventory inquiry and React purchase-order screen
Covers controls that break workflow agents: controlled inputs, search dialogs, result selection, date fields, query results, dynamic grid rows
Framework-neutral semantics: prefer labels, roles, and state changes over generated DOM paths
Evidence before completion: verify the postcondition of an action, not just a successful click
Synthetic by default: no vendor-specific ERP adapter, credentials, execution logs, or production memory
Playwright regression suite verifies popup visibility, form state, and exact row-count change
Roadmap: Vue and Web Components samples, popup patterns, empty query results, nested grids, framework-neutral action/evidence schemas, benchmark plans
Design principles: framework-neutral semantics, evidence before completion, synthetic by default, regression first, small and inspectable

Observable outcomes: lookup trigger must produce visible dialog; selection reflected in originating form; row-add increases table by exactly one row; controlled input retains value after state updates; equivalent actions testable across frameworks
Useful even without an AI planner: fixture library for Playwright, locator research, QA training, automation regression testing

Standard HTML inventory workflow: select warehouse, open item search dialog, query ITEM-001, select exact result, confirm dialog closes, verify reflection in main form, set item type/date/stock status, query, verify result table, add one row, verify row count increased by exactly one

Judgment rules: resolve controls by label/role/stable ID/test ID before coordinates; distinguish dialog Query button from main-form Query by active dialog scope; do not treat successful click as completion without postcondition; empty settled query result is valid zero-result outcome
Stop/report conditions: control not identifiable, dialog not visible, item not reflected, row count not increased by exactly one, destructive/external submission required

React purchase-order workflow: enter order date, select account type, open vendor search modal, query Wonjin, select exact V001·Wonjin result, confirm dialog closes, verify reflection in read-only vendor field, set procurement type, enter notes and verify React state retains value, add one detail row, verify row count +1, bind item/quantity/urgent to new row

Judgment rules: scope dialog controls to visible role=dialog surface; dispatch normal browser input/change events so React controlled state receives updates; bind detail inputs to the row created by current Add row action
Stop/report conditions: controlled input does not retain value, vendor dialog not visible, vendor not reflected, new detail row not identifiable, destructive/external submission required
Public workflow plans demonstrate same sample workflows in English and Korean for localization comparison
Plans separate inputs, workflow steps, judgment rules, completion evidence, and stop/report conditions
No login or screen-navigation section because sample URL opens target screen directly
All values synthetic and safe for public testing

stats.fact: WorkCanvas Studio is a TypeScript project created 2026-08-13, last updated 2026-09-02, with 2 stars and 0 forks on GitHub
Requires Node.js 22 or later; quick start is git clone, npm install, npx playwright install chromium, npm run dev, then open http://127.0.0.1:5173/
The public edition contains two applications: a Standard HTML inventory inquiry screen and a React purchase-order screen
Four public workflow plans ship in the repo: standard-html-inventory and react-purchase-order, each in English and Korean
The Standard HTML inventory plan uses input data: warehouse Seoul Warehouse, item ITEM-001, item type Raw material, base date 2026-08-04, stock status Available, include zero stock false
The React purchase-order plan uses input data: order date 2026-08-04, account type Raw material, vendor Wonjin, procurement type Domestic purchase, item PART-001, quantity 10, urgent false
Both interactive samples include an English/Korean language selector; automation-facing IDs, test hooks, and control values remain stable across languages
npm test builds the React sample and runs browser tests against both frameworks; npm run capture:demos regenerates public screenshots and source recordings

angles: Framework-neutral semantics: labels, roles, and state changes over generated DOM paths — the core differentiator for AI agents that must work across Standard HTML and React
Evidence before completion: verify postconditions (dialog visible, selection reflected, row count +1) rather than treating a successful click as success
Synthetic-by-default design: reproducible failures without exposing private URLs, credentials, or production data — safe for agent evaluation and regression testing
The exact controls that break workflow agents: controlled inputs, search dialogs, result selection, date fields, query results, dynamic grid rows
Bilingual (English/Korean) samples with stable automation IDs across languages — useful for localization testing of agents
Roadmap gaps as future content hooks: Vue and Web Components samples, empty query results, nested grids, framework-neutral action/evidence schemas, benchmark plans
